questions.prompt: A material has \(Y=150\,\mathrm{GPa}\) and yield stress \(300\,\mathrm{MPa}\). Find the yield strain in the linear elastic model.
Define plastic deformation in one sentence.
questions.answer: Plastic deformation is deformation that is not fully recovered after the load is removed.

questions.prompt: A part has yield stress \(240\,\mathrm{MPa}\) and safety factor \(3.0\). Find the allowable working stress.
A \(18\,\mathrm{kN}\) tensile load is carried by a material with yield stress \(360\,\mathrm{MPa}\) using safety factor \(2.5\). Find the minimum area from yield alone.
A material is loaded elastically to stress \(80\,\mathrm{MPa}\). Its Young modulus is \(160\,\mathrm{GPa}\). Find the elastic strain.
A stress-strain graph is linear up to \(\sigma_y\), then no longer follows the original line. Which stress is associated with first permanent deformation: yield stress or ultimate stress?
questions.answer: First permanent deformation is associated with yield stress. Ultimate stress is associated with the maximum stress before failure, not the start of plastic deformation.

questions.prompt: A specimen is loaded to stress below yield and then unloaded. Explain what happens to its strain and why.
questions.answer: If the stress stays below yield and the material behaves elastically, unloading follows the same linear path back to zero stress and zero strain. No permanent strain remains.

questions.prompt: A material with \(Y=100\,\mathrm{GPa}\) is loaded to total strain \(3.0\times10^{-3}\). On unloading, it follows slope \(Y\) from a maximum stress of \(200\,\mathrm{MPa}\). Find the permanent strain.
questions.answer:
The elastic strain recovered during unloading is
\[
\epsilon_{\mathrm{recovered}}=\frac{\sigma_{\max}}{Y}=\frac{200\times10^6}{100\times10^9}=2.0\times10^{-3}
\]
Permanent strain is
\[
\epsilon_p=3.0\times10^{-3}-2.0\times10^{-3}=1.0\times10^{-3}
\]

questions.prompt: A rod of area \(A\) and length \(L\) is loaded to force \(F_{\max}\) beyond yield. At maximum load its measured total strain is \(\epsilon_{\max}\), and unloading is linear with slope \(Y\). Derive the permanent extension after unloading, state assumptions, and interpret the special case \(F_{\max}/A=Y\epsilon_{\max}\).
questions.answer:
Assume uniform stress, unloading is linear with slope \(Y\), and the rod returns to zero stress after unloading. At maximum load,
\[
\sigma_{\max}=\frac{F_{\max}}{A}
\]
The recoverable elastic strain during unloading is
\[
\epsilon_e=\frac{\sigma_{\max}}{Y}=\frac{F_{\max}}{AY}
\]
The permanent strain is
\[
\epsilon_p=\epsilon_{\max}-\frac{F_{\max}}{AY}
\]
Therefore the permanent extension is
\[
\Delta L_p=L\left(\epsilon_{\max}-\frac{F_{\max}}{AY}\right)
\]
If \(F_{\max}/A=Y\epsilon_{\max}\), then \(\epsilon_p=0\). The loading point lies on the elastic line, so the deformation is fully recoverable in this model.

questions.prompt: A tensile member must carry load \(F\), remain below yield stress \(\sigma_y\) with safety factor \(S\), and extend by no more than \(\delta_{\max}\) over length \(L\) with Young modulus \(Y\). Derive the symbolic minimum area and state which constraint controls in each parameter regime.
questions.answer:
Yield with safety factor requires
\[
\frac{F}{A}\le\frac{\sigma_y}{S}
\]
\[
A\ge A_y=\frac{FS}{\sigma_y}
\]
The stiffness requirement is
\[
\delta=\frac{FL}{YA}\le\delta_{\max}
\]
\[
A\ge A_\delta=\frac{FL}{Y\delta_{\max}}
\]
Both constraints must hold, so
\[
A_{\min}=\max\left(\frac{FS}{\sigma_y},\frac{FL}{Y\delta_{\max}}\right)
\]
Yield controls when
\[
\frac{FS}{\sigma_y}\ge\frac{FL}{Y\delta_{\max}}
\]
The extension limit controls in the opposite regime. The controlling constraint is the one demanding the larger area.
